justification: Investigating DQ-88 (item #3 of the user's own priority list) surfaced a real, independent silent-failure bug: services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py never read stale_since/stale_reason from housing_sepp_standards, unlike services/cdc_screen.py's identical, working W3 (#839) contract for cdc_eligibility_standards. Every CDC/ADG-eligibility answer this engine computes could serve a standard the legislation monitor had already flagged as amended, with zero surfaced notice. Fixed the read-side gap, registered a new live check (DQ-96) for the write-side backfill gap that remains, and corrected an inflated, unsupported figure in DQ-88's own tracker text. Not Critical: no application code path changed behaviour for any CURRENTLY non-stale row (all 45 housing_sepp_standards rows read stale_since IS NULL today, so this fix is currently a no-op in production until either a row goes stale or the write-side backfill lands) -- this is additive plumbing of an existing, unused DB column, not a behaviour change to today's served answers. Not Minor: it is a real code fix with new tests, not a wording-only change.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards.stale_since/stale_reason already exist (added by #839, 2026-07-29) and are already written by scripts/legislation_monitor.py's mark_dependent_standards_stale(). No new column, no new table. _fetch_standards_grouped() already selects 4 sibling columns (source_clause/document/url/effective_date) from the same table with the identical query shape.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed (from DQ-88's own tracker text) that SEPP Housing 2021 backs 241 served provisions. Checked live, not assumed: v2_marker ILIKE housing/sepp = 0 rows, document_id-linked regulatory_provisions = 12, ref_number text match = 1. The 241 figure does not check out against any query and traces to an unrelated '241-row zone repair' elsewhere in the same tracker file -- corrected in DQ-88's row text.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Pure additive: 2 new Optional[str]=None dataclass fields on FormEligibility, 2 new columns in an existing SELECT, 2 mirrored fields on the existing HousingSeppFormOutput pydantic contract (kept in lockstep by test_housing_sepp_contract_locks_the_dataclass_fields, which caught the omission on first run). No new function, no new table, no new query beyond extending one existing SELECT.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no external call in this change; the underlying legislation-monitor amendment detection (external, against legislation.nsw.gov.au/PCO) was already verified real in the DQ-88 investigation this branch is based on (instrument_registry.last_changed/current_version measured live).
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- no frontend code touched. The two new fields flow through services/upzoning_check.py's existing dataclasses.asdict() serialization with no additional wiring; a frontend consumer would need its own follow-up to render the notice, not part of this fix.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before this fix: a planner asking for CDC/Housing-SEPP eligibility on a lot got an answer computed from a standard the legislation monitor had already flagged as amended 2026-04-24, with no indication anything might have changed -- exactly the class of silent staleness the W3 mechanism was built to prevent, but only for one of its two dependent tables. After this fix: the notice is available as structured data (stale_since/stale_reason) on every FormEligibility result whenever a row IS marked stale; today (no row is yet stale) this is a no-op, verified live-neutral.

functions.name: _fetch_standards_grouped
functions.input: none (reads DATABASE_URL env var, queries housing_sepp_standards)
functions.output: dict keyed by development_type; each value now additionally carries stale_since (raw datetime or None) and stale_reason (str or None), latest stale_since wins paired with its own reason
functions.if_none: no matching rows for a dev_type -> that key absent from the returned dict, unchanged from before this branch; DB unreachable -> exception propagates to evaluate_eligibility's try/except, which logs and returns [] (fail-safe, unchanged from before)

break_it.scenario: The latest-wins comparison in _fetch_standards_grouped compares a raw datetime against a previously-stored isoformat STRING on a later iteration, raising TypeError.
break_it.what_happens: First draft of this fix did exactly this -- caught immediately by running the new tests, which failed with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'isoformat' before the bug could reach any real code path.
break_it.how: Kept stale_since as a raw datetime throughout the grouping loop (matching the comparison's own type), converting to isoformat only once, at the point _result() builds the FormEligibility instance -- mirrored exactly on services/cdc_screen.py's own established pattern for the identical problem (Sol #839).
break_it.repro: tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py::test_fetch_standards_grouped_pairs_stale_date_with_its_own_reason exercises two rows for the same development_type with different stale_since values and asserts the later date pairs with its own reason.

break_it.scenario: Adding 2 fields to FormEligibility without updating its pydantic mirror (HousingSeppFormOutput in services/intelligence_brief.py) would silently desynchronise the two contracts.
break_it.what_happens: A future brief-layer consumer trusting HousingSeppFormOutput's field set would never see the new stale notice even after the dataclass gained it -- the exact 'brief silently stopped surfacing X' class of bug this repo's own field-coverage/contract-drift tooling exists to catch.
break_it.how: Caught immediately by test_housing_sepp_contract_locks_the_dataclass_fields failing on the first full-suite run; fixed by adding the same 2 fields to HousingSeppFormOutput and re-running brief_field_coverage_ratchet.py --regen.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_brief_golden_fixtures.py -k contract_locks -- passes now; reverting the intelligence_brief.py change reproduces the original failure.
